newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends down in kerb, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends down in kerb, seen falling.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed 0.14 down at 40.30 to the dollar in brisk kerb trade on Monday amid fear of rupee depreciation, dealers said.
They said the dollar demand was rising due to concern that the rupee might lose more value against the U.S. currency.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on September 10, was 36.9700/37.1549 to the dollar.
The premium on the foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 8.70 percent compared to 8.60 percent at the opening.
